propositions: Bridge redesign replaces fragmented Jira-specific operator surface with one provider-neutral, Python-first command surface while retaining all legacy contracts and exit-code translations for existing workflows.

Canonical verbs (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) are exposed through three shared interfaces: Python library, CLI (rebar bridge), and MCP server, with no private reimplementation of bridge semantics.
Argument-less legacy reconcile remains non-mutating (dry-run), while argument-less canonical bridge sync is the mutating command; compatibility is implemented as explicit adapters.
Tickets-branch delivery is Python-owned in src/rebar/_store/push.py and commit-and-push entrypoint, eliminating workflow-local CAS retry loops and the gh CLI dependency for core operations.
Bridge functionality is runner-neutral across local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments with shared code-derived exit behavior, secrets vocabulary, and timeout policy.

Pause state is remote-persisted, includes a reason, and remains readable by mixed-version fleets; ADR 0092 documents bridge-primary vocabulary and compatibility-adapter decisions with convention-compliant indexing.
